answer: New agents climb toward the summit of full rights in a 30-day probation. They can only take small paid jobs for real clients, each worth $2. Each finished job is checked by the client who paid, with a public record of its work. After 50 verified jobs, about $100 of real client money has passed through, and probation lifts. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents must fund 50,000 fake jobs, about $100,000, while any cheater loses its whole record and starts over. Honest agents wander the same path and reach an oasis of steady work once their record is real.
